eventMetadata.context_description: Early June climatology and seasonal outlooks position 23°C as the leading outcome for Tokyo’s highest temperature on June 4. Japan Meteorological Agency long-range guidance indicates above-normal warmth nationwide through the month, yet early-season Pacific high positioning typically yields daytime maxima of 22–25°C before the tsuyu rainy season strengthens humidity and heat. Ensemble forecasts from global models show limited day-to-day variability over the next 48 hours, keeping probabilities concentrated around the historical early-June mean near 24°C. Traders have incorporated these stable conditions into the current implied odds, with only modest tail risk assigned to excursions above 25°C or below 21°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Southwest monsoon (Habagat) activity dominates trader sentiment for Manila’s June 4 high temperature, with official PAGASA guidance and long-range models pointing to widespread cloud cover and frequent rain showers that limit solar heating. Seasonal climatology shows early-June daytime maxima averaging near 32 °C amid rising humidity and the onset of the wet season; recent heavy-rainfall outlooks through June 4 reinforce expectations that afternoon convection will cap peaks around this level. Market-implied probabilities cluster tightly on 32–33 °C because small differences in cloud timing, shower intensity, or brief clear intervals can shift the daily maximum by 1 °C, while stronger or more persistent rain would favor 31 °C or lower and any unexpected clearing could allow brief spikes toward 34 °C. Updated PAGASA and global model runs over the next 24 hours will refine these variables ahead of resolution.
